summary: DST rollover induced quota-refill drift causing soft 429s across geo-edge pools
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-08 02:00 UTC we observed increased soft 429s (rate-limit responses) for BrightCart's dedicated pool across eu-west and us-east. Impact: customer reports degraded throughput for order-processing chat assistants during peak morning traffic, 5-15% request failure rate for short-lived streams. Observed behavior: token refill counters on edge nodes drifted by up to 65 seconds relative to origin refill windows after a scheduled BGP failover that coincided with a DST clock adjustment in eu-west. This led to temporary double-accounting and then under-refilling on some edge pools, producing tenant-level soft 429s. Timeline: 02:00 UTC scheduled BGP rotation -> 02:05 first 429 spikes -> 02:12 engineered mitigation (edge token smoothing) applied -> 02:40 error rates returned to baseline but drift persisted until manual smoothing rollout.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer with dedicated pool and multi-region edge enabled uses many short-lived streaming sessions (avg duration 8s) around the local DST rollover window.
2) Trigger a BGP-driven edge failover or proxy swap during the clock change (simulated by forcing NTP step on an edge node).
3) Observe refill-window misalignment between origin and affected edge nodes; measure per-edge token refill timestamps and tenant refill deltas.
4) Send high-concurrency short streams from a client farm (concurrency 500-800) to replicate tenant-level soft 429s.

comments: 2026-03-08 02:10 - Support (Maya Patel): Customer reports intermittent 429s during morning traffic spike after our scheduled network maintenance. Asking to escalate; customer SLA is enterprise/dedicated.

2026-03-08 02:18 - Eng (Liam O'Connor): Initial hypothesis: refill-window drift due to NTP step at edge combined with BGP swap. Checking refill epoch alignment and edge token accounting traces. Triage: Sev1, page on-call infra.

2026-03-08 02:35 - SRE (Anika Rao): Deployed temporary smoothing (refill_splay=30s) to affected edges for BrightCart; observing drop in 429 rate from ~12% to ~2% over 20 minutes. Continuing to monitor.
2026-03-10 09:00 - Support (Maya Patel): Customer acknowledged mitigation; requested follow-up on permanent fix and assurance this won't affect billing token counts.
investigation_notes: Edge nodes that experienced NTP step reported refill epoch offsets (see logs).
BGP failover caused some clients to rehome to different edge pools; combined with short stream patterns, token window exhaustion cascaded faster than expected.
Rate-limiter assumes monotonic epoch alignment; small negative time steps can cause transient double-decrement behavior in our pre-check path.
Billing counters appear consistent with net token consumption after reconciliation; however per-edge temporary negative cache adjustments were applied and need audit.
Reproducibility: reproduced in staging by forcing time step and BGP swap; confirmed refill drift and soft 429 spike for short session workloads.
resolution: Mitigation applied: rolled out refill_splay smoothing to affected edge clusters and banned NTP step during network maintenance windows as a temporary operational control. Long-term plan: modify rate-limiter to use monotonic clock where available and add cross-edge epoch reconciliation on join. Created follow-ups for infra and billing audit.
resolution_notes: Follow-up actions assigned: INT-331210 (infra) to implement monotonic-clock guard; INT-331211 (billing) to verify token accounting reconciliation for BrightCart's invoice window; postmortem page created at linked Confluence URL. Customer offered 10% credit for incident window; finance notified.
